original_topic: empirical reply-to-proposition alignment in email and dialogue, focusing on partial replies, multiple questions, unanswered questions, and multi-proposition antecedents
topic: empirical reply-to-proposition alignment in email and dialogue, focusing on partial replies, multiple questions, unanswered questions, and multi-proposition antecedents
focus: academic gaps of the previous round

prior_gaps.description: Direct empirical evidence is still missing for proposition-level agreement, rejection, approval, clarification, and answer scope in authentic workplace email or enterprise chat, especially cases where one short response applies to only part of a preceding message.
prior_gaps.suggested_search_query: "reply scope" email dialogue proposition agreement approval rejection workplace communication

prior_gaps.description: The corpus does not establish a validated annotation and evaluation scheme for mapping workplace responses to exact proposition or span targets while representing exact, partial, ambiguous, unsupported, discontinuous, and potentially multiple antecedents.
prior_gaps.resolution_notes: Define a task-specific annotation schema over msgloom data with explicit target-span or proposition identifiers and labels for exact, partial, ambiguous, unsupported, discontinuous, and multi-antecedent cases. Produce annotation guidelines, double-annotate a representative benchmark, measure inter-annotator agreement, adjudicate disagreements, and evaluate candidate resolvers with per-class precision, recall, calibration, and abstention metrics. Existing discourse and coreference schemes can inform the design, but validation of the concrete msgloom representation is an engineering benchmark task.

prior_gaps.description: Direct evidence remains insufficient for aligning replies to one or more questions when a preceding workplace message contains multiple questions, requests, or alternatives, including detection of questions that remain unanswered.
prior_gaps.suggested_search_query: "question answer alignment" dialogue "multiple questions" partial answer unanswered questions

prior_gaps.description: It remains open whether and how a workplace response should be modeled as targeting a composite or multi-proposition antecedent. The corpus supports composite abstract discourse referents theoretically and multi-antecedent entity reference analogically, but provides no direct evaluation of multi-proposition reply scope in work communication.
prior_gaps.suggested_search_query: "multi-antecedent" propositional anaphora dialogue composite discourse referent reply

prior_gaps.description: The appropriate abstention, ambiguity, and missing-antecedent policy for msgloom has not been validated. In particular, the relative cost of an over-broad approval or commitment link versus leaving a link unresolved is a product-risk assumption that requires an explicit cost model and dedicated benchmark rather than being inferred from these papers.
prior_gaps.resolution_notes: Define an application-specific loss matrix for false broad links, false narrow links, incorrect antecedents, and abstentions, with higher penalties where incorrect links can create approval or commitment state changes. Build a benchmark enriched for ambiguous, missing-antecedent, and partial-scope cases; calibrate confidence thresholds on a validation split; compare forced-linking against selective prediction and abstention policies using expected cost, coverage-risk curves, calibration error, and high-severity error counts.

rounds.topic: reference resolution to propositions and the semantic scope of replies in work communication
